shots.composition_notes: Locked-off wide two-shot of the widow and the tall funeral-suit character standing at the graveside, shot through an out-of-focus white-flower arch in the extreme foreground (top-left and bottom corners). Characters are placed center-right of frame, both facing screen-right toward off-frame gravestones/mourners; headroom is generous above their heads leaving open sky. A blurred mourner is visible at the far right edge, cropped by the frame. The floral foreground never moves or refocuses, confirming a static camera for the full 5.9s despite three dialogue lines playing over it.

Hard cut to a static close-up on the woman's face and upper torso, camera roughly at eye level. She is framed left-of-center with the man's nose/chin entering hard-focus from the right edge of frame, his black coat sliver visible bottom-right — an over-the-shoulder-style crowd without showing his full face. Headroom is tight, cropping just above her hair bun.

Single-frame whip/rack-focus insert: the man's jaw and nose tip fill the left of frame in soft focus while background elements blur further; a blurred mourner is visible upper right. Functions as a jump-cut flash rather than a held shot, syncing to the word 'DON'T' before snapping back to the previous close-up composition.

Returns to the identical static close-up framing used at 5.9-6.73s (same eye-line, same crop on the woman's face and shoulders with the man's nose intruding from the right). Held through 'DON'T...MORTGAGE.' with no reframing — the brief insert frame at 6.73-6.93s reads as a stutter/flash cut inside what is otherwise one continuous held composition.

Static close-up on the man's droopy-eyed face centered in frame with a gold 'LOW BATTERY PEOPLE' title card and 'CREATED BY NIN.' credit overlaid across the lower nose/mouth area; his frown is left fully visible above the text, giving the branding a deadpan reaction-shot backdrop.

Full black-background end card, no live-action/animated framing — static graphic layout with the show logo centered and a yellow 'NEW EPISODE DAILY' tape banner beneath it, both vertically centered in the lower half of the 9:16 frame.

framing_patterns_notes: The video relies on exactly two setups for the entire joke: a static wide establishing two-shot (seen through a blurred flower foreground frame) that holds for nearly half the runtime while multiple lines of setup dialogue play over it, then a single hard cut to a tight static close-up on the reacting character (the woman) that is held for the punchline delivery, briefly interrupted by a one-frame rack-focus insert on the other character's face for emphasis on 'DON'T.' There is no camera movement anywhere in the piece (no pans, tilts, zooms, or handheld shake) — all shot changes are hard cuts between static setups, and the framing shift from wide to close-up is itself used as the escalation device leading into the punchline.
